text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- New unit to be created by Lyonnaise des Eaux and Suez merger expects turnover to top 180 billion francs.
-- World trade shows poor performance for 1996, partly due to currency distortions.
-- France Telecom to unveil tariffs offered to competitors to lease its phone lines.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe announces creation of a bank for small and medium-sized businesses, which would have a fund of one billion francs over two years.
-- Renault takes over control of its Argentina plant and remains majority shareholder in unit to operate its Brazilian business.
-- EU commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy rules out delaying implementation of a European single currency.
-- Merger, takeover trend continues among Paris brokerages
-- Former Fiat chairman Giovanni Agnelli says Bundesbank's choice of countries allowed to join single currency will partly be a political choice.

-- Workers at Renault assembly plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium, to resume work on Monday, despite vote by a third of workers against it. Six-week strike was protesting Renault's decision to shut down the plant.
-- Two-third of Renault Vilvoorde workers vote to return to work.
